devdoc.details: This contract does NOT determine whether a person has died.         It relies on an authorized executor (or, in the extended         version, a set of verifiers) to attest that the real-world         condition for inheritance has been satisfied. This is a         deliberate design choice made to address the blockchain         "oracle problem" honestly rather than pretend it can be         solved on-chain.

params._executor: Address authorized to initiate the inheritance process.
params._timelockDuration: Waiting period, in seconds, between initiation        and the earliest possible distribution (e.g. 30 days = 2592000).

devdoc.title: Digital Inheritance Management Prototype

addBeneficiary(address,uint256).notice: Adds a beneficiary. Total allocation across all beneficiaries         must equal exactly 100% (10000 basis points) before assets         can be distributed. This is checked at distribution time,         not at add time, so beneficiaries can be added incrementally.

cancelInheritance().notice: Allows the owner to cancel an in-progress inheritance during         the timelock window, for example if the executor triggered         it incorrectly and the owner is, in fact, still able to act.

depositAssets().notice: Deposits native ETH into the contract to be distributed         according to the beneficiary percentages once inheritance         is executed.

executeInheritance().notice: Executes the distribution once the timelock has elapsed.         Callable by anyone (executor or a beneficiary) so that the         process does not depend on a single party remaining online;         the amounts are already fixed by the beneficiary percentages,         so the caller has no discretion over the outcome.

initiateInheritance().notice: Called by the executor once they have verified, through an         off-chain process, that the real-world condition required         for inheritance (e.g. confirmed death of the owner) has         been satisfied. This does not distribute assets immediately;         it starts the timelock.

removeBeneficiary(uint256).notice: Removes a beneficiary by index. Only allowed while the plan         is still ACTIVE (i.e. before the executor has triggered         inheritance).

setDocumentReference(string).notice: Stores a reference (e.g. an IPFS CID or a document hash) to an         encrypted off-chain document. The document itself is never         stored on-chain, only a pointer/fingerprint for integrity         verification.

setExecutor(address).notice: Reassigns the executor address. Only while the plan is ACTIVE.

updateBeneficiaryShare(uint256,uint256).notice: Updates the percentage allocated to an existing beneficiary.

userdoc.notice: Academic prototype demonstrating programmable, timelocked         distribution of digital assets to predefined beneficiaries.
